clue.text: The crossword game enjoyed on board

definitions.text: The crossword game enjoyed on board

parts.words: The crossword game enjoyed on board
parts.note: a word game in which players build interlocking words, crossword-fashion, with lettered tiles laid on a board

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a crossword while travelling on a ship or train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a passenger doing a crossword on a voyage; in fact it describes a game literally played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known board game of making words from lettered tiles is played in a crossword-like grid.

clue.text: Intelligence from Troy — as. Icelanders might call it?

definitions.meaning: wisdom and shrewdness

definitions.text: Troy — as. Icelanders might call it?
definitions.meaning: Icelanders are famous for their sagas, so they might call a legendary city like Troy a city of sagas

explanation.surface: Wisdom comes from ancient Troy, as Icelanders might say.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into two words: the Norse saga, and the city of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd wisdom is a synonym; and Troy, the setting of an epic tale, is jokingly a city of legend.

clue.text: Being irregular, I re-enlist with spring

indicators.note: irregular letters are out of order, so I re-enlist is rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier who had served irregularly re-enlists in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but means bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back, which is the meaning of resilient.

clue.text: Tom's sort of study

parts.note: the hero of Tom ___'s Schooldays shares a surname with the colour in a phrase meaning a reverie

explanation.surface: What kind of study does Tom do?
explanation.walkthrough: A brown study is a daydream; Tom Brown's Schooldays is Thomas Hughes's novel of English public-school life.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour gives both the surname of Hughes's schoolboy and the idiom for absent-minded reverie.

clue.text: Room entered through the French window

indicators.note: the room enters the French word, going inside it

parts.note: le is French for the
an attic is a room under the roof

explanation.surface: Someone enters a room through the French window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French window' looks like one item; 'the French' gives LE and 'window' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A window of criss-crossed strips with small panes is called a lattice window.

clue.text: Fairy flycatcher

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream bears this name
a spider's web traps flies

explanation.surface: A fairy who catches flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare named a fairy after the spider's silky trap, which catches insects.

clue.text: Rambling rose, white under different conditions

indicators.note: rambling wanders, so the letters of rose white wander out of order

explanation.surface: A white rambling rose.
explanation.walkthrough: A rambling rose is a climbing plant; here 'Rambling' rearranges ROSEWHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: In other circumstances is an exact synonym of otherwise.

clue.text: Grace, initially embaces little boy-incorrectly

indicators.note: printed thus for embraces: the cricketer's initials hold the boy's name

parts.note: the cricketer W G Grace was known by his initials
Ron is a short form of the boy's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A girl called Grace hugs a small boy in the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a girl's first letter; it is W G Grace, the Victorian cricketer, whose initials WG embrace RON. The paper printed 'embaces' for embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: Done amiss can be expressed as done wrong, the adverb use of the word.

clue.text: Forbidden to listen to the musicians

indicators.note: listen to signals the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: It is forbidden to listen to the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Prohibited and outlawed are synonyms.

clue.text: A stand-in, by intruding, is very good -

indicators.note: the word for by intrudes into the word for a stand-in

parts.note: sub is short for substitute
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A substitute who pushes in is said to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a substitute player barging in; 'intruding' signals the container, and 'per' is Latin for by.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and splendid are synonyms.

clue.text: Enthusiasm got us in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so the words got us are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our zeal landed us in a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges GOTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish and zest are synonyms of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Land worth some points

definitions.meaning: to come to earth, as an aircraft does
in American football a score of six points, also a try in rugby

explanation.surface: Property that is worth a few points on some scale.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football, carrying the ball over the opponents' goal line scores six points.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's arrival on the runway and a scoring play in American football share this term.

clue.text: Cleaned out — in hiding — what a bloomer!

indicators.note: the word in is hiding inside the rearranged letters
out signals that the letters of Cleaned are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's money has been cleaned out while they were lying low, which was a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a bungled burglary; 'out' rearranges the letters of Cleaned and 'hiding' tucks the word in among them. A bloomer is both a blunder and, as a pun, a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lesser celandine is a yellow spring wildflower, so it blooms.

clue.text: Bad lad, but a sport

definitions.meaning: a rascal or scoundrel
in biology a sport is a plant or animal that deviates from its type

explanation.surface: A boy who misbehaves but is a good sport about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' here is the biologist's word for an abnormal specimen, not a game or a good-natured person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scoundrel; a rogue plant is an off-type variant, which breeders call a sport.

clue.text: Sweet diet for Elsie, Lacie and Tillie

definitions.meaning: a sugary syrup, so something sweet

definitions.text: diet for Elsie, Lacie and Tillie
definitions.meaning: in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters by these names who lived at the bottom of a well and ate its syrup

explanation.surface: Three girls are fed a sugary diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The names come from the Dormouse's tale at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup's darker cousin is a sugary food, and Carroll's sisters lived in a well of it.

clue.text: … as hands go from time to time

definitions.text: as hands go from time to time

parts.words: as hands go from time to time
parts.note: the hands of a timepiece move from one hour to the next in a particular direction

explanation.surface: This is how hands go, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' looks like 'occasionally', but describes the hands on a dial moving from one time to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The direction a dial's hands turn names the way rightward rotation is described.

clue.text: Nap's back as a card game

definitions.text: Nap's back as a card game

parts.words: Nap's back as a card game
parts.note: nap is an old card game; the clue playfully names another card game for partners that has replaced it in popularity

explanation.surface: The old game of nap has returned to favour.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap (from Napoleon) is a trick-taking card game; another, more famous partnership trick-taking game is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership trick-taking game with bidding is the best-known card game of its kind.

clue.text: Whip up an egg — one twice is — featured in experiments

indicators.note: whipping an egg beats it about, so these letters are mixed
the letter for one is used two times

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipe: whisk an egg, then whisk it again, as in a kitchen experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' rearranges UPANEGG plus II, the latter from 'one twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent often used in laboratory tests gives its name to any experimental subject.

clue.text: Valentino's present-day namesake

parts.note: the silent-film idol was called Rudolph; so is a famous animal of Christmas, the day of presents

explanation.surface: A modern-day actor named after Valentino.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolph Valentino was a silent-film star; 'present-day' means Christmas Day, when presents are given, not modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph, Santa's red-nosed sleigh-puller, shares the silent star's first name.

clue.text: Hit someone in a row

definitions.meaning: a blow
the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace in a racing boat

explanation.surface: Someone in a quarrel lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is rowing, as in a boat race.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a synonym; and the oarsman who sets the rhythm in a racing eight bears this title.

clue.text: "That two-handed — at the door" (Milton)

parts.note: a line from Milton's Lycidas with one word missing, the machine that stands ready to smite once

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in Lycidas continues 'Stands ready to smite once, and smite no more.'
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's mysterious instrument of judgment is a device or machine.

clue.text: From Lister I learnt the meaning of aseptic

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the run of words Lister I learnt

explanation.surface: A student learns the meaning of aseptic from the surgeon Joseph Lister.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, which makes the scene apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs, as surgical instruments must be.

clue.text: A citizen's theme

definitions.meaning: someone owing allegiance to a monarch or state
the topic of a discussion

explanation.surface: A citizen's chosen topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A national under a crown and the topic of a talk share this word.

clue.text: Four is one, honest!

definitions.meaning: four is two times two, a number of this kind
fair and above board

explanation.surface: Someone insists that four is one, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four is one' sounds false until you see it means four is a number of a certain kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times two makes a perfect power-of-two number; and fair dealing is described with the same word.

clue.text: Fast living

definitions.meaning: speedy
an old sense, as in 'the ... and the dead'

explanation.surface: Living life in the fast lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy is a synonym; and the old phrase 'the quick and the dead' uses it for those alive.

clue.text: Drive lands member in bad lie

indicators.note: the member goes inside the jumbled letters
a bad version of lie is one with its letters jumbled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A golfer's drive lands in a bad lie.
explanation.walkthrough: A lie in golf is where the ball comes to rest, which makes the surface a golfing scene; 'bad' jumbles the letters and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To push forward or propel is a synonym of drive.

clue.text: Novel character leaves Japanese game contenders unnamed

annotationWithheld.why: Novel character leaves Japanese game contenders unnamed (2-7): GO (Japanese game) and the Hartley novel are clear, but no reading accounts for 'character leaves' and 'contenders unnamed' as BETWEEN; scan and search give no other text
annotationWithheld.clue: Novel character leaves Japanese game contenders unnamed

clue.text: Times item (not the leader) very good

indicators.note: the first letter of item is removed

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good

explanation.surface: A Times article, not the lead story, is very good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means musical speeds; PI is old slang for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the musical term for speed or pace gives musical times.

clue.text: 'Apparatus I can entangle in fruit …

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: entangled letters are mixed up, so the words I can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being able to tangle a device up inside fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangle' jumbles the two short words I can, and 'in' puts the jumble inside the fruit, between its fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or machine, especially a household one, is an appliance.

clue.text: … that's found cored by many a" tree

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: a cored fruit loses its middle, so the central letter is removed

parts.note: that refers back to the fruit of the previous clue

explanation.surface: Continues the last clue: the fruit is found with its core removed by many a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 27; 'that' is the fruit, APPLE, which 'cored' reduces to APLE by losing its middle P.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore family includes this tree, whose leaf is on Canada's flag.

clue.text: I am inclined to listen to her

indicators.note: listen to signals that the words are said aloud

parts.note: to be inclined is to lean, so I am inclined is I lean

explanation.surface: Someone admits they tend to listen to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am inclined' looks like 'I tend to', but is the physical sense, I lean, which sounds like a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name can stand for any female person, and 'her' points to such a name.

clue.text: Part-time journalist as member of the framework

definitions.meaning: a freelance correspondent paid by the piece
a longitudinal structural beam in a frame, as in a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: A freelance reporter belongs to some organisational setup.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance local correspondent and a lengthwise structural beam share this name.
